text:
J.T. Compher missed most of October and has been one of Detroit's steadier forwards since coming back, with four points in a four-game stretch (CBS Sports) and the Detroit Free Press writing that he and Michael Rasmussen are finally playing to the Red Wings' standard.

He has six points in 11 games, and Detroit has 56% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice. The team has scored 4.3 fewer goals than those chances deserve when he's out there, so his assists are, if anything, light.

That matters more than usual in Detroit this season. Dylan Larkin is refusing to play until he's traded, which pushes more of the center work onto players like Compher, a Stanley Cup winner with Colorado in 2022. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries and taking 53% of his shots off the rush last season. Our projection sees about 31 points from here.
